hints: Focus on the two separate reactions in sequence, first ester hydrolysis with NaOH, then the triiodomethane test.
Remember that refluxing an ester with NaOH gives a carboxylate salt plus an alcohol, so list the alcohol formed from each of 1, 2 and 3.
Recall which alcohol structures give $\text{CHI}_3$, ethanol and any $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}$ group, then check which esters supply one of those.
walkthrough:
**Recognise ester hydrolysis**

All three substances are esters, $\text{RCO}_2\text{R'}$. Reflux with aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ hydrolyses them.

$$\text{RCO}_2\text{R'} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{RCO}_2^-\text{Na}^+ + \text{R'OH}$$

**Recall the iodoform test**

Alkaline aqueous iodine gives a pale yellow precipitate of triiodomethane, $\text{CHI}_3$, with a specific group.

Positive groups are $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}$. In practice this means ethanal, methyl ketones, ethanol $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ and secondary alcohols of type $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)R}$.

**Work out the alcohol from each ester**

1: $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2^- + \text{CH}_3\text{OH}$. Methanol has no $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}$ unit, so negative. Ethanoate also does not give $\text{CHI}_3$.

2: $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2^- + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. Ethanol is oxidised under the test conditions and gives $\text{CHI}_3$, so positive.

3: $\text{HCO}_2\text{CH(CH}_3)_2 \rightarrow \text{HCO}_2^- + \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$. Propan-2-ol contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}$, so positive.

**Combine to find M**

Only esters 2 and 3 produce an alcohol that forms the pale yellow precipitate. Ester 1 does not. Therefore the correct combination is 2 and 3 only.

options.A: States 1, 2 and 3 are all possible. This is wrong because 1 gives methanol plus ethanoate, neither of which contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}$ unit needed for $\text{CHI}_3$.
options.B: States 1 and 2 only. This is wrong because 1 is negative and 3 is missed. Students choosing this often think any $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2$ ester gives a positive test, forgetting the test comes from the alcohol part, not the ethanoate part.
options.C: States 2 and 3 only. Ester 2 gives ethanol which gives $\text{CHI}_3$, and ester 3 gives propan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, which also gives $\text{CHI}_3$. Ester 1 gives only methanol, which is negative.
options.D: States 3 only. This correctly includes propan-2-ol from 3 but wrongly excludes 2. Ethanol from ester 2 is also a classic positive result for alkaline aqueous iodine, so the answer is incomplete.
